title: rescue-ai-repair-catalog
description: Typed, reviewed catalog of repair actions for one domain. The AI may only propose action_id values from these files; it never produces commands. Every command is a fixed argv array whose placeholders are whole elements bound to typed, validated parameters. Cross-field invariants (risk vs. rollback/backup, placeholder declarations, unique IDs across files) are enforced by scripts/lib/repair_catalog.py.

expect_line.description: Python engine only (android platforms): after a zero exit the combined output must contain one line exactly equal to this text (control characters stripped, outer whitespace trimmed). It may end in one {enum_param} placeholder. A mismatch fails the step (verify-failed). The line comes from the catalog, never from data.

type.description: enum: one of values. integer: minimum..maximum. block_device: an internal disk or partition chosen by the operator and re-checked by the engine (never the rescue USB). target_root: mount point of the target_ref OS, provided by scripts/lib/target_mount.py. package_name / service_name: strict patterns, never starting with '-'. state_dir: an engine-provided subdirectory (values: clamav or quarantine) of the USB state directory. detection_ref: an opaque d-N reference to one entry of the local malware detection list (never evidence); the engine resolves it to a verified regular file path. android_device: the Android phone named by the proposal's target_ref (and-N), resolved by the Python engine at execution time from the current USB inventory and adb (authorized, same opaque id as the evidence) to the integer transport id for `adb -t`; never operator, evidence or model input. fastboot_device: the same for a phone in fastboot mode, rendered as the `usb:<port>` selector that `fastboot -s` accepts (never the serial). fastboot_slot: engine-provided, the active A/B slot (a or b) read from the phone right before the action, for rollback. firmware_file: an operator-supplied absolute path (values: exactly one of image or zip) that the engine opens without following a final symlink, size-bounds, hashes and passes to the child as an inherited file descriptor; it needs a sha256 parameter named <name>_sha256 and only that SHA-256 is journaled. sha256: 64 hex characters supplied by the operator. printer_ref: the CUPS queue of the printer named by the proposal's target_ref (prn-N), resolved by the Python engine at execution time by running the printer discovery again (same opaque id as the evidence, network printers only when the operator opted in); the queue name exists only inside the child argv and is never shown or journaled. bundle_root: the rescue bundle directory, used only as {name}/scripts/lib/... for a closed list of shipped fixed files. bundle_config: one fixed configuration file of the bundle's config/ directory (values: exactly one name from a closed list, e.g. freshclam-user.conf), usable only as --config-file={name}; the engine renders the bundle path, never an operator, evidence or model path.

target_families.description: OS families this action applies to (checked against target_systems[].family of target_ref). Omit for actions about the machine itself (hardware).

risk.description: safe: no persistent change or a harmless one (self-test, service restart, module reload); the only class auto-safe may run without a prompt. reversible: persistent change with an automatic rollback step. irreversible: a change that cannot be undone but loses nothing that is stored (paper and ink used by a test page or a head cleaning, queued print jobs discarded); no rollback, no backup, always asks (never auto-safe, even when a trigger proposed it), and a lp action is never proposed by a trigger or by the model. destructive: may lose data; needs a backup reference, a typed approval, and a manual or restore-backup rollback.

requires_target_rw.description: Live mode only: the target OS must be remounted read-write (explicit approval, never auto-safe).

triggers.description: Evidence checks that make the engine propose this action (origin catalog-trigger). Empty: only an AI proposal or the operator can select it.

guards.description: Engine-native checks that run after approval and before any step (Python engine only; the actions never apply to the host launchers). A failed guard journals a precondition failure with a typed reason and runs nothing. bootloader-unlocked: fastboot getvar unlocked must be yes (else bootloader-locked). image-matches-device: the firmware zip's android-info.txt require board/product lines must match fastboot getvar product (else identity-mismatch). single-download-mode-device: exactly one Samsung download-mode device is on USB and it is the proposal's and-N with the evidence's opaque id.
